name: Eyes on the Nile
tagline: Monitor crops and water across the Nile Delta so farmers can save water and spot crop stress early.
briefing: The Nile Delta feeds tens of millions of people, and every drop of water counts. Design a satellite that watches crop health and water use, so farmers know where and when to irrigate. You have $120M, a 2-year minimum mission, and a launch slot in 3 years.
learningGoals: Match the orbit to the observation (same lighting every day)
Balance instrument data with your radio link
userSegment: Farmers, irrigation engineers and water ministries across the Nile Delta

twins.name: Landsat 9
twins.fact: Images the whole Earth in visible, infrared and thermal bands; used worldwide to track crops and water.

twins.name: Sentinel-2
twins.fact: A pair of satellites revisiting every 5 days with 13 colour bands for vegetation monitoring.

name: Storm Watcher
tagline: Watch dust storms and flash floods over Africa and the Middle East around the clock.
briefing: Dust storms and flash floods can strike Africa and the Middle East within hours. Forecasters need an eye in the sky that never looks away. Watch continuously for at least 5 years.
learningGoals: Why geostationary orbit stares at one region
Delta-v: the spacecraft must finish its own orbit raising
Long missions need margins for aging
userSegment: Weather forecasters, civil-protection agencies and airlines

twins.name: GOES-16
twins.fact: Watches the Americas from geostationary orbit; carried the first lightning mapper in GEO.

twins.name: Meteosat Third Generation Imager-1
twins.fact: Watches Europe and Africa from GEO with an imager and a lightning imager.

name: Ice Hunter
tagline: Map water ice in the Moon's permanently shadowed craters to choose landing sites for future crews.
briefing: Future lunar crews need water for drinking, breathing and rocket fuel. It may be frozen in craters near the Moon's south pole that never see sunlight. Map it to help choose safe landing sites.
learningGoals: Trading rocket cost against launch margin
userSegment: Mission planners choosing safe, water-rich landing sites for future crews

twins.name: Lunar Prospector
twins.fact: Its neutron spectrometer found signs of hydrogen, a hint of ice, at the lunar poles.

twins.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
twins.fact: Maps the Moon with a laser altimeter, a thermal radiometer and a neutron detector.

name: Red Relay
tagline: Study methane and dust in the Martian atmosphere while relaying data home for rovers on the surface.
briefing: Two jobs at once: study methane and dust in the Martian atmosphere, and relay data home for the rovers on the surface. Mars is unforgiving: weak sunlight, minutes of radio delay, and launch windows only every 26 months.
learningGoals: Solar power falls with distance from the Sun
userSegment: Planetary scientists and the rover teams whose data you relay

twins.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
twins.fact: Studies Mars with a high-resolution camera and spectrometers, and relays rover data to Earth.

twins.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
twins.fact: Hunts for methane in the Martian air and relays data for surface missions.

twins.name: MAVEN
twins.fact: Studies how Mars lost its atmosphere, and also relays rover data.

name: First Light
tagline: Fly an infrared telescope to see the first galaxies and the atmospheres of distant planets.
briefing: Light from the first galaxies has travelled for over 13 billion years and arrives as faint infrared heat. Fly a telescope cold and steady enough to catch it.
learningGoals: Why some telescopes go to L2
Big science, big budget: protecting the reserve
userSegment: Astronomers studying the first galaxies and the atmospheres of distant planets

twins.name: James Webb Space Telescope
twins.fact: A 6.5 m gold-coated infrared telescope at L2, shaded by a tennis-court-size sunshield.

twins.name: Herschel Space Observatory
twins.fact: A far-infrared telescope at L2 that studied how stars and galaxies form.

name: Sandbox
tagline: No grades, no limits: build anything and watch what happens.
briefing: No grades, no limits. Build anything and watch what happens.
learningGoals: Break things on purpose and read the report
